capitals.name: Charles Fort (Rupert House)
capitals.note: The HBC page: 'founded, in 1668, the first fort on Hudson Bay, Charles Fort' (Rupert House, 1668). Not called a capital by the page; used as the first seat of the company. Coordinates are the researcher's.

capitals.name: York Factory
capitals.note: Rupert's Land page: 'The company was based at York Factory'; the HBC page dates the post to 1684. The company's head office was in London; the court of 1839 sat at Red River (District of Assiniboia). Coordinates are the researcher's.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The 1670 charter gave 'sole Trade and Commerce' of the bays, rivers and adjacent lands 'not held by other Christian princes' and called them 'Rupert's Land'; the page says the southern border ran 'west of Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains' as a drainage divide until 1818. This is a chartered claim: the company held coastal posts (Charles Fort 1668, Moose Factory 1673, York Factory 1684) and the French held James Bay and Hudson Bay posts 1686-1713 except Fort Albany. Infobox area 3,861,400 km2; this gazetteer shape is about 5.3 M km2 (ratio 1.37, the gazetteer region overshoots into Alberta and Nunavut), within the factor of two. Draw soft. fx-32 (F185): the North Dakota part is cut to the Hudson Bay drainage side of the Missouri divide (the Rupert's Land page: 'The southern border, west of Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains was the drainage divide' until the Convention of 1818 substituted the 49th parallel), so the Missouri-drained west and south of the state, which is Louisiana, is not drawn as Rupert's Land; the polygon is the researcher's reading (confidence 1). spanish-louisiana subtracts the same land.

The Convention of 1818 ceded 'all of Rupert's Land south of the 49th parallel and east of the Continental Divide' to the United States, so the Canadian-side Hudson Bay drainage remains. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the 1821 merger the company administered the North-Western Territory under British licence beside its chartered Rupert's Land; the NWT page says it was 'not technically within the area of land granted to the Hudson's Bay Company in May 1670'. Drawn as one HBC domain because the Canada dossier treats both as one 1870 transfer. The Columbia District in the Oregon Country (jointly occupied by Britain and the United States until 1846) is not drawn: the monopoly there was a trading right, not territory. No area on either page. Area check: this shape is about 7.3 M km2 by cell count (7.7 M km2 by cell area) against the 3,861,400 km2 the Rupert's Land page gives for Rupert's Land alone (ratio 1.9-2.0); the excess is the North-Western Territory added here (not part of the 1670 grant) and the gazetteer region's overshoot into Alberta and Nunavut.

region.text: the Hudson Bay drainage, 'from the Atlantic to the Rocky Mountains, and from the prairies to the Arctic Circle'

ledger.note: 1670: Charles II grants the Hudson's Bay Company its charter. The company was incorporated 'on 2 May 1670' as 'The Governor and Company of Adventurers of England, trading into Hudson's Bay'; the Rupert's Land page adds that the charter gave 'the sole Trade and Commerce of all those Seas, Streights, Bays, Rivers, Lakes, Creeks, and Sounds' and declared the lands 'one of our Plantations or Colonies in America, called Rupert's Land'.

region.text: the James Bay posts (Moose Factory, Rupert House) taken by the Chevalier de Troyes; Fort Albany stayed English

ledger.note: 1686: the French raid the bay. 'In March 1686 the French sent a raiding party under the Chevalier de Troyes' against the James Bay posts; the company held little of the shore until the Treaty of Utrecht.

region.text: the James Bay posts at the foot of the bay, except Fort Albany

ledger.note: 1686: the James Bay posts fall. The HBC page says the French 'retained all of the outposts except Fort Albany until 1713'; the page does not list the posts lost in 1686 one by one.

region.text: York Factory on the Nelson-Hayes estuary

ledger.note: 1694: the French take York Factory. d'Iberville 'captured York Factory in 1694, but the company recovered it the next year.'
1695: the company recovers York Factory ('the company recovered it the next year').

1697: d'Iberville again takes York Factory. 'In 1697, d'Iberville again commanded a French naval raid on York Factory'; the page dates the Battle of Hudson's Bay to 5 September 1697 and does not name the Treaty of Ryswick.

region.text: the posts and shores of Hudson Bay and James Bay held by France since 1686

ledger.note: 1713: Hudson Bay returns to Britain. On 11 April 1713 France 'ceded Nova Scotia and its claims to Newfoundland and territories in Rupert's Land'; the HBC page adds that Hudson Bay 'again became a British possession'.
1713: the Hudson Bay fighting ends with the Treaty of Utrecht (11 April 1713).

'By order-in-council dated 23 June 1870' the British government admitted the territory to Canada, and 'Canada asserted control on 15 July 1870'; the company had surrendered its charter on 19 November 1869 under the Rupert's Land Act 1868 and received 300,000 pounds.

wars.name: Hudson Bay raids of the Anglo-French rivalry
wars.outcome: France took the James Bay posts in 1686 and York Factory in 1694 and 1697 (the company recovered it in 1695) and kept all the outposts except Fort Albany until the Treaty of Utrecht returned the bay to Britain in 1713.
wars.note: No Wikipedia war article was opened; the HBC page gives the raids ('In March 1686 the French sent a raiding party under the Chevalier de Troyes'; 'The Battle of Hudson's Bay' on 5 September 1697) and the Utrecht page the 1713 cession. The wider wars (Nine Years' War 1688-1697, War of the Spanish Succession) are named by the HBC page only for 1697.

certainty.note: A chartered claim to a drainage basin: no survey, only coastal posts; the French posts of 1686-1713 on James Bay and Hudson Bay are the exception in detail only.

The southern border is sharp along the 49th parallel from the Convention of 1818 (Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains); the boundaries with the North-Western Territory, with Russian America and with Labrador stay approximate.

notes: Rupert's Land is not a Cliopatria row. Written as the company's chartered domain (the Hudson's Bay Company lands), type colony, family britain. Pages opened: Rupert's Land, Hudson's Bay Company, Convention of 1818, North-Western Territory, Treaty of Utrecht, Stikine Territory, Colony of British Columbia 1858-1866 (seven). Not on the pages: any dated post beyond Charles Fort 1668, Moose Factory 1673, York Factory 1684 (and Fort Albany, undated); the 1763 Treaty of Paris and the Quebec Act's effect on the Labrador/Hudson Bay boundary; the end date of the 1821 licence (1859); the Red River Colony grant of 1811; the Oregon Treaty (the Columbia District is left out because the monopoly there was a trading right). The French raids are recorded as events of this state with new-france as counterpart; the new-france dossier pairs the contest with english-colonial-empire, so the two ledgers use different counterpart strings for the same bay. The Canada dossier uses 'hudson-s-bay-company-lands' for this state. Region names the gazetteer lacks: North-Western Territory (drawn as Yukon + Northwest Territories + northern British Columbia north of 56 N; the report lists it); the Stickeen Territories and the 1863 BC enlargement are drawn by polygons from the Stikine Territory page (62 N, 125 W, Nass-Finlay line). The Rupert's Land gazetteer region is the Canadian-side Hudson Bay drainage and overshoots in Alberta and Nunavut (its own note).
